x: sqcart — Functional Specification Status: Draft Applies to: the sqcart component, all targets sqcart::read , sqcart::write , sqcart::lua , sqcart bootstrap Does not specify: the container format that is normative in the format spec or generator behaviour that is the engine services' concern 0. Related documents Document What it specifies sq cartridge 2.0.md The .sq container format — bytes, layout, manifest schema. Normative. sqcart component.md Where sqcart sits architecturally — placement, layering, bootstrap rule, dogfood chain. sqcart/include/sqcart/sqcart.hpp The concrete C++20 API — exact signatures. tools/sqcart isolation.fish The build time gate that enforces §2.4 of this document. This document What the software does — testable requirements, tracing to the format spec, ready to drive test suite construction. This document does not restate wire format rules. Where a requirement here exists because of a format spec rule, it cites the section §3.3 , etc. rather than repeating it. Terminology — Cartridge, Reader, Writer, Payload, Kind, and the RFC 2119 keywords MUST/SHOULD/MAY — is as defined in the format spec §2. Requirement IDs use the scheme FR <AREA <N . They are stable identifiers: once assigned, an ID is never reused for a different requirement, even if the requirement is later removed. 1. Purpose and scope 1.1 Purpose This document enumerates, as atomic and testable statements, what sqcart does in response to every input it can be given. It exists so that: an implementer can build against numbered requirements rather than prose; a test author has a checklist, not a guess, for what the test suite needs to cover; a reviewer can ask "which FR does this diff satisfy" and get an answer. 1.2 Scope In scope: everything the four sqcart targets do — opening, validating, reading, digesting, extracting and writing cartridges, plus the Lua binding and the bootstrap CLI. Out of scope, and deliberately absent from every requirement below: resource resolution, dependency graphs, version solving engine services, §2.4.3 of the Generator Architecture ; generation, template processing as behaviour , workflow sequencing; cross cartridge conflict detection — e.g. whether two different kits' declared integration areas collide is an engine question §2.7.4 , not a question sqcart answers about one cartridge in isolation; signature verification and trust policy format spec §10, reserved ; target overlay resolution format spec §11, reserved ; network access of any kind, anywhere. A function is out of scope for sqcart if the Squared framework runtime — which has never heard of a template, a kit, or a generation pipeline — would have no use for it. This is the same test sqcart/AGENTS.md gives human reviewers, restated here as the boundary of this document. 2. Overall description 2.1 Product perspective sqcart answers one question — is this a valid cartridge, what does it declare, and what are its bytes — and nothing downstream of that answer. 2.2 Consumers Consumer Links Typical operations squared pg engine Resource, Template, Kit, Package, Asset Services sqcart::read open, validate, read entries, inspect kind bodies Squared framework runtime sqcart::read open a cartridge kind archive at application startup, read the entry point, extract payload Platform launcher Android/Termux sqcart::read open, inspect manifest for presentation metadata, extract Packaging tooling / CI sqcart::read + sqcart::write pack, verify, digest, list squared pg Lua workflows and standalone scripted tools sqcart::lua same operations, from Lua Release engineering sqcart bootstrap CLI pack/list/verify before a working generator exists 2.3 Operating environment Termux on arm64 android and desktop Linux, both with a C++20 toolchain. std::expected C++23 is not assumed available; see expected.md . No network access is assumed or used at build, test, or run time §1.13 of the Repository Conventions . 2.4 Constraints FR CON 1. No file under sqcart/ SHALL include anything outside the sqcart/ tree. FR CON 2. sqcart/CMakeLists.txt SHALL configure, build, and pass its tests with no parent tree present. This is enforced mechanically by tools/sqcart isolation.fish , not by convention alone. FR CON 3. No backend type mz zip archive , yyjson doc , or equivalent SHALL appear in any header under sqcart/include/ . FR CON 4. No exception SHALL cross the public API boundary. Every fallible public operation returns Result<T . FR CON 5. squared pg SHALL link sqcart from vendored source at build time and SHALL NOT acquire it as a .sq cartridge component spec §2 . No requirement in this document may be satisfied by a design that requires a cartridge reader to read the cartridge containing the cartridge reader. 2.5 Assumptions and dependencies miniz and yyjson are available, either vendored under sqcart/third party/ or supplied by the host build per SQCART USE EXTERNAL . The host filesystem may be case sensitive or case insensitive; sqcart MUST behave correctly under both format spec §3.3 . Unless a function is explicitly documented otherwise, sqcart types are not internally synchronised: concurrent const access is safe, concurrent mutation is not. 3. Functional requirements 3.1 Opening a cartridge — Cartridge::open , Cartridge::open memory FR OPEN 1. open SHALL accept either a .sq archive or an exploded directory containing a readable SQ INF/manifest.json , and SHALL detect which form it was given without requiring the caller to specify format spec §3.5 . FR OPEN 2. open SHALL default to Conformance::strict . FR OPEN 3. Under strict conformance and an archived cartridge, open SHALL reject an archive whose first entry is not SQ INF/manifest.json stored with method 0 format spec §3.2 , returning container invalid . FR OPEN 4. open SHALL run the validation pipeline in the order defined by format spec §12.1 up to and including stage 8 payload presence . Stage 9 compatibility resolution SHALL NOT be performed by open ; it requires a resolution context sqcart does not have. FR OPEN 5. On the first pipeline stage that fails, open SHALL return the corresponding Result failure and SHALL NOT proceed to later stages. Failures are not accumulated across stages. FR OPEN 6. open memory SHALL apply identical validation to open . The returned Cartridge SHALL be valid only for the lifetime of the caller supplied span ; this is a documented precondition, not a runtime checked one. FR OPEN 7. Under Conformance::lenient , open SHALL perform only stages 1–4 of §12.1 container, paths, limits, manifest well formedness . Stages 5–8 SHALL be skipped, and any violations they would have caught SHALL instead surface later, if at all, as diagnostics from validate §3.9 rather than as an open failure. 3.2 Path validation — validate entry path , internal to open / extract to FR PATH 1. A path SHALL be rejected with path unsafe if it: has a leading / ; contains a . or .. segment; contains NUL, a backslash, a : drive designator, or a C0/C1 control character; is empty; or except a tolerated directory entry ends in / — per format spec §3.3. FR PATH 2. Within one cartridge, two entries whose paths differ only by ASCII case, or only by Unicode normalisation form, SHALL both be rejected with path unsafe , even though neither path is independently invalid. FR PATH 3. A path exceeding Limits::max path bytes or Limits::max path depth SHALL be rejected with limit exceeded , not path unsafe — the two error codes are distinguished by cause, not merely by outcome, so a caller can tell "malicious" from "too big." FR PATH 4. validate entry path SHALL be usable standalone, without an open Cartridge , applying exactly the same rules as path validation performed during open and Writer::add . A writer preparing entries before a container exists SHALL be able to rely on this function alone. FR PATH 5. Path validation SHALL occur before any byte of the corresponding entry is read into memory. A cartridge with one invalid path among ten thousand valid ones SHALL fail at path check time, not after partially decompressing the archive. 3.3 Resource limits — Limits FR LIM 1. Every limit in format spec §3.4 SHALL be enforced with the specified default when the caller does not override OpenOptions::limits . FR LIM 2. No limit SHALL be disableable by setting it to zero or an unbounded sentinel; a Limits field of 0 SHALL be treated as "reject everything" for that dimension, not "no limit." FR LIM 3. Compression ratio limits max entry ratio , max archive ratio SHALL be evaluated using declared sizes from the central directory before full decompression begins, so that a crafted small archive claiming an enormous uncompressed size is rejected without first attempting to allocate or decompress that size. FR LIM 4. Exceeding any limit SHALL produce limit exceeded and SHALL NOT produce a partially materialised result — no directory created, no file written, for that operation. 3.4 Manifest parsing — Manifest::parse , Cartridge::manifest FR MAN 1. The manifest SHALL be parsed as UTF 8 without a byte order mark; a leading BOM SHALL cause manifest malformed . FR MAN 2. A manifest missing any envelope field marked REQUIRED in format spec §5.1 format , format version , kind , id , version SHALL cause manifest malformed . FR MAN 3. A manifest whose format is not exactly "squared cartridge" SHALL cause manifest malformed , not format unsupported — the latter is reserved for a recognised format at an unsupported version. FR MAN 4. A manifest whose format version this build does not implement SHALL cause format unsupported , at parse time, before any other member is read . This build implements exactly 2 . There is no compatibility path for format 1 in either direction. FR MAN 5. kind SHALL be validated for shape only: one identity segment matching a z a z0 9 . A malformed token SHALL cause kind invalid . An unrecognised token SHALL NOT: this library does not enumerate the ecosystem's roles, and a cartridge of a kind it has never seen SHALL open, index and report normally format spec §5.2.1 . Retired. This requirement previously rejected a manifest carrying a body that did not match its kind . There are no kind bodies to be foreign, and a consumers section addressed to a namespace that is not yours is the mechanism working, not a masquerade. FR MAN 6. consumers sections SHALL be carried without interpretation. A conforming implementation SHALL check that consumers is an object, that each key is a well formed consumer identity, and that each value is an object; it SHALL check nothing else about a section's contents. Manifest::consumer SHALL return the section as JSON text with member order preserved, and Manifest::consumers SHALL enumerate identities. An absent section SHALL be reported as absent and never synthesised as empty format spec §5.6 . FR MAN 7. Unrecognised members of any manifest object SHALL be ignored, not rejected format spec §5.4, default tier , and SHALL remain retrievable via Manifest::raw json . FR MAN 8. Every token in requires features SHALL be checked against OpenOptions::supported features . If any declared token is absent from the supplied set, open SHALL fail with feature unsupported naming the missing token, and SHALL NOT partially honour a manifest whose critical requirements are not fully met. FR MAN 9. Manifest::parse SHALL accept a manifest in isolation, without a surrounding container, applying the same rules as manifest validation during open . FR MAN 10. The structural constraints a manifest must satisfy SHALL match docs/developer/specs/schema/sq manifest 2.schema.json exactly, whether or not the implementation runs that schema literally. A manifest the schema accepts and sqcart rejects, or vice versa, is a defect in whichever side disagrees with the schema — the schema is the tie breaker. 3.5 Kind bodies — retired FR KIND 1 through FR KIND 5 required this library to know a template's ownership globs, a kit's integration areas, an asset entry's path, a cartridge's permission default and a Lua entry's bytecode target. Every one of them was a rule about a consumer's schema, and holding them here is what made format spec §0.1 false in code: a framework runtime linking this library acquired the generator's vocabulary whether it wanted it or not. They are not weakened or relocated within this document. They are the consuming project's requirements now, verified by its own conformance tests. What this library owes a consumer is FR MAN 6: the section arrives intact, addressed, and unopened. The loss is real and worth naming. FR KIND 3 in particular — every declared asset path is present in the cartridge — was a genuinely useful check that nothing here replaces. A consumer can make it better, because it knows what the reference was for. 3.6 Entry access — entries , contains , find , read , read into FR ENTRY 1. entries SHALL return every payload and SQ INF/ entry in a stable order for a given cartridge — the central directory order for an archive, and lexicographic path order for an exploded directory — such that two calls against the same unmodified cartridge return identical sequences. FR ENTRY 2. contains and find SHALL return false / nullptr for a syntactically invalid path rather than raising an error; path validity is a precondition of open , already satisfied for every entry the cartridge actually holds, so a query for an impossible path is simply a miss. FR ENTRY 3. read SHALL return the complete decompressed content of an entry or fail; it SHALL NOT return a truncated buffer under any circumstance, including when the entry exceeds Limits . Exceeding the limit SHALL fail with limit exceeded before any bytes are copied to the caller. FR ENTRY 4. read into SHALL fail if out is smaller than the entry's uncompressed size, and SHALL NOT write any bytes into out in that case — no partial writes. FR ENTRY 5. Reading an entry whose declared CRC 32 does not match its decompressed content SHALL fail with container invalid , distinct from integrity failed , which is reserved for SQ INF/hashes.json mismatches specifically. 3.7 Integrity — content digest , declared digests , verify integrity FR INT 1. content digest SHALL implement format spec §9.2 exactly: SHA 256 over path LF hex sha256 content LF lines, entries sorted byte wise ascending by path, excluding SQ INF/hashes.json and everything under SQ INF/signatures/ . FR INT 2. content digest SHALL be independent of the archive's compression method and compression level. Two archives with identical payload content but different deflate settings SHALL produce identical digests. FR INT 3. declared digests SHALL parse SQ INF/hashes.json into an EntryDigestMap and SHALL return resource error via container invalid or manifest malformed as appropriate if the file is present but malformed. If the file is absent, declared digests SHALL return an empty map, not an error — absence of declared digests is not itself a fault. FR INT 4. verify integrity SHALL recompute the digest of every entry named in declared digests and fail with integrity failed , naming the first mismatching entry, on any disagreement. FR INT 5. When SQ INF/hashes.json is absent, verify integrity SHALL succeed vacuously there is nothing declared to contradict . A caller requiring mandatory integrity checking SHALL check declared digests for non emptiness itself; sqcart does not invent a requirement the format does not impose. Flagged for review — see §10. FR INT 6. OpenOptions::verify integrity = true SHALL apply the same rules as an explicit verify integrity call, performed during open before it returns successfully. 3.8 Extraction — extract to FR EXT 1. extract to SHALL re validate every entry path immediately before writing it, independently of validation already performed at open time. This defense in depth SHALL hold even though it is provably redundant for a cartridge that passed open unmodified — it exists for cartridges opened under Conformance::lenient and for any future code path that constructs a Cartridge without going through the full pipeline. FR EXT 2. extract to SHALL NOT write any file outside dest under any input, including a manifest or entry list crafted after a successful but lenient open . FR EXT 3. With overwrite = false the default , extract to SHALL fail before writing anything if any destination path already exists — the check SHALL precede all writes, not interleave with them. FR EXT 4. extract to is not itself transactional across multiple entries: on a mid extraction failure, entries already written SHALL remain on disk, and the returned error SHALL identify the entry that failed. Callers requiring all or nothing semantics across a whole extraction — as the engine's Transaction Service does per format spec §2.3.13 — SHALL wrap extract to in their own staging and rename strategy. sqcart does not duplicate the engine's transaction model. FR EXT 5. extract to SHALL NOT restore Unix permission bits, symbolic links, or any other external file attribute recorded in the archive, per format spec §3.1's rule that such attributes carry no meaning in v1. 3.9 Validation pipeline — validate FR VAL 1. validate SHALL run stages 1–8 of format spec §12.1 and SHALL NOT attempt stage 9 compatibility resolution . FR VAL 2. ValidationReport::conforming SHALL be true if and only if diagnostics contains no entry of Severity::error . FR VAL 3. An unrecognised file under SQ INF/ SHALL produce a Severity::info diagnostic and SHALL NOT affect conforming . FR VAL 4. For a template kind cartridge, validate SHALL check that every path materialisable from tree/ matches exactly one of ownership.generated / .user / .shared ; a path matching zero or more than one SHALL produce a Severity::error diagnostic naming the path and the conflicting classifications. FR VAL 5. validate operates on one cartridge in isolation. It SHALL NOT accept, and SHALL NOT require, information about any other cartridge. Detecting that two independently selected kits' declared integration areas collide is out of scope for this function — see §1.2 — and no future revision of this requirement may add a multi cartridge parameter to validate ; that capability belongs in an engine service. 3.10 Error reporting FR ERR 1. Every fallible public function SHALL return Result<T . Any internal C++ exception SHALL be caught and converted to an Error before crossing the public API boundary; none SHALL propagate to the caller. FR ERR 2. Error::id SHALL be populated whenever the manifest parsed successfully, even if a later pipeline stage is what ultimately failed — for example, payload missing after a valid manifest SHALL still carry the cartridge's id . FR ERR 3. Error::entry SHALL be populated whenever the failure is attributable to one specific entry, and SHALL be absent when it is not e.g. format unsupported , which is a property of the whole manifest . FR ERR 4. Error::recoverable SHALL be set per the following table, reflecting whether an alternative workflow action is meaningfully available at the point of failure: Code Recoverable Rationale container invalid false Nothing to salvage path unsafe false Security boundary limit exceeded false Input rejected outright manifest missing false No cartridge to act on manifest malformed false No cartridge to act on format unsupported true A different version may satisfy the caller feature unsupported true A fallback path may exist kind invalid false Wrong kind for the request payload missing false Cartridge is internally inconsistent native code prohibited false Security boundary integrity failed false Trust boundary io failed true Often transient internal false Library defect; not the caller's to fix 3.11 Writer SQCART ENABLE WRITER FR WRITE 1. Writer::create SHALL truncate an existing file at out only once finish is called successfully; a Writer that is never finished SHALL NOT leave a partial file at out . FR WRITE 2. set manifest SHALL apply the full manifest validation of §3.4–§3.5 before accepting the manifest, and SHA

sqcart My Vision for sqcart Squared .sq cartridges will act as high capacity, high performance data containers that can support both enormous datasets and executable extensions. Reference implementation of the Squared Cartridge Specification 2.0 docs/developer/specs/sq cartridge 2.0.md — the .sq container format used for Squared templates, kits, packages, asset bundles, plugins and distributable applications. Standalone C++20. No dependency on squared pg or on the Squared framework. Build Or, without CMake handy on Termux : Embedded, with the host supplying the backends: Targets Target Option Default For sqcart::read — always every consumer sqcart::write SQCART ENABLE WRITER ON packaging tools sqcart CLI SQCART ENABLE CLI top level only humans and CI sqcart::lua SQCART ENABLE LUA OFF deferred; no consumer yet A game runtime or Android launcher links sqcart::read alone and carries no compressor, no canonical ordering logic and no manifest serialiser. Library sqcart implements the container and the manifest envelope. It carries consumer sections without interpreting them, which is what lets the same library serve squared pg and the Squared framework runtime without either acquiring the other's vocabulary spec §0.1, §5.6 . .sq archives and exploded directories containing SQ INF/manifest.json are both accepted; open detects which, and the two are semantically equivalent spec §3.5 down to producing the same content digest. CLI Exit codes: 0 success, 1 operation failed, 2 usage error, 3 cartridge is non conforming. verify is usable as a CI gate unchanged. stdout carries machine readable results only; diagnostics go to stderr. The digest is computed over content and paths, never over archive bytes, so it is stable across compressors and across container forms. C++20 and std::expected <expected is C++23. include/sqcart/expected.hpp aliases std::expected where available and supplies a minimal substitute otherwise. Code using sqcart::Result<T compiles either way; tests/test expected.cpp asserts the two paths behave identically. Constraints See AGENTS.md for the scope rule, the CLI's IO isolation rule, and the single digest implementation rule. Run ../tools/sqcart isolation.fish before committing.

sqdrive The Virtual Cartridge Drive: the big file interface for squared apps. Mount a Squared Cartridge 3.0 https://github.com/squared netizen/sqcart and read and, from phase 3, write files of any size by range. sqcart is the only thing that writes the format; the Drive builds on it and owns staging, caching, commit policy and recovery. sq.drive : the C++23 module apps link import sq.drive; . sqdrive : the command line tool. A Drive is thread safe, and the File s it opens outlive it. Reads go through a cache of decoded chunks 1 MiB each, or a whole entry that is not chunked , least recently used first out, bounded in bytes and keyed by content, so an unchanged chunk stays cached across commits. Writing. A read write mount holds sqcart's writer lock until it unmounts a second one gets Code::busy . Writes change 1 MiB chunks in memory; sync appends what changed to the journal in the staging folder one per cartridge, never beside it and flushes it, and the synced chunks leave memory: they are read back from the journal. Past memory bytes a write syncs first, so memory stays bounded however much is staged. Entries without the w flag are not changed §4.2 . Committing. A commit freezes what is staged, starts a new journal segment for the writes that go on meanwhile, and hands the frozen changes to sqcart as one commit, naming again every chunk no write touched; only a write to a path being committed waits for it. With the budget policy the default commits run on a thread of their own, past commit bytes or once the oldest change is commit after old, and at unmount; with explicit only only on commit ; with on unmount also at unmount. Past staging bytes a write waits for a commit budget or gets Code::limit . Files the Drive makes are stored chunked, so later commits write only the chunks they change. After a commit with nothing else staged, the Drive compacts the cartridge §10.4 when compact min bytes and compact at of it are unreachable; writers wait meanwhile, readers do not. wait waits for background commits and reports one that failed. After a crash , the next read write mount reads each journal segment up to its last sync whose checksum passes a torn tail is dropped and: The cartridge is The Drive at the segments' commit replays them all; it commits as the policy says one commit on, with the time a segment wrote down before committing knows that commit landed: drops that segment and those before it, replays the ones after anywhere else another writer committed refuses with Code::conflict , or, with discard journal , sets the segments aside as journal.conflict <time .<n On Android, and in sqterm An app. Android stops an app that leaves the screen, and may end its process without another word. squared already says when: the platform calls Application::background on Android's stop sq::App gives its model a turn there to save . That is where a Drive's changes are made safe: sync is quick an append and a flush , and what it wrote is replayed at the next mount if the process is ended before a commit. A budget Drive commits it on its own in the meantime; nothing more is needed. Mount with .staging in the app's private storage squared's FileSystem::local folder , not shared storage. sqterm. pkg install sqdrive sqterm's packages/sqdrive , built from a tag of this repository with clang 23 against sqterm's sysroot and runtimes packages . Its journals go in ~/.local/state/sqdrive , or $SQDRIVE STAGING . Building Needs clang and libc++ with import std; ; 23 is what sqterm and CI use. Offline: sqcart's library and what it builds with are vendored in third party/sqcart tools/vendor sqcart.sh ../sqcart copies it again, with its PINNED , and built first into build/sqcart . Where it stands The phases of the design: 1. sqcart additions sqcart 8 : renames, resizes, many ranges per commit, streamed puts, compaction under the writer's lock. Done. 2. Read only Drive sqdrive 1 . On a 200 MB chunked file on a container's disk: sequential reads about 200 MiB/s; a random 4 KiB read that misses the cache costs about 3 ms, most of it SHA 256 over the 1 MiB chunk it verifies a faster SHA 256 is the next thing to win . 3. Writing and the journal sqdrive 2 . 4. Background commits and bounds sqdrive 3 . A 256 MiB file streamed in 256 KiB writes at staging bytes 24 MiB and memory bytes 4 MiB keeps both under their bounds, committing 8 MiB at a time as it goes the design's 2 GiB gate, scaled for CI . A commit reads the chunks it writes from the journal sqcart's put range file , so while it runs it holds none of them in memory. 5. x: sqmake: draft specification Status: draft 0.1, 2026 11 19. Nothing here is built yet. What this specification decides is marked as decided; what it only proposes is marked as proposed, and the open questions are listed at the end. It grows from the research note "sqpg Build System: Research and Recommendations" 2026 11 16 and the SDK's plan for one C++23 toolchain 2026 11 19 . 1. What sqmake is sqmake is the squared SDK's build system. It builds an application from a workspace: it knows how to build, not what a workspace is. sqpg creates a workspace, square manages it, and sqmake builds it; sqmake asks square what to build square build inputs and knows nothing else about workspaces. It keeps make's model targets, prerequisites, a target rebuilt when what it is made from changes and drops make's syntax. It runs the build itself: it never writes make, CMake or Ninja files for another tool to run. 1.1 Requirements decided Small and self contained. One binary with a library behind it; no JVM, no Python, no daemon. It runs on the phone, in sqterm, as well as on a desktop or CI. Offline. A build makes no network request and downloads nothing. Programmable. Lua 5.4 describes builds; other programs use sqmake as a library libsqmake . Explainable. sqmake build explain prints the whole resolved graph and every command it would run. Nothing sqmake infers is hidden. A strong reason for every concept make does not have. 1.2 Where its ideas come from Idea From In sqmake The engine Ninja A graph run in process, with command hashes and compiler written header dependencies The front door Cargo Conventions and a short declarative description: most projects need almost no build code The escape hatch Cargo's build.rs , Zig's build.zig Real code, in Lua, for what conventions miss; no second language Usage requirements CMake A library declares what its users need include paths, flags, modules , and linking it applies them 2. The model 2.1 Targets, rules and commands decided A target is a file sqmake makes. It has inputs files, and other targets and one command that makes it from them. A rule is a Lua function that, given inputs and an output, returns a command. A command is an argument list: a program and its arguments, run without a shell, so there is no quoting and no shell syntax. 2.2 When a target is out of date decided A target is rebuilt when any of these holds: 1. it does not exist, or an input is newer than it; 2. its command's hash differs from the last time it was built; 3. a header its compile read has changed the compiler's dependency file, MMD MF , records which ; 4. a module it imports has been rebuilt §5 ; 5. the toolchain's fingerprint §4.2 differs from the one it was built with. The fingerprint is part of every command's hash, so a new compiler or C++ library rebuilds what it compiled even when the command line reads the same. What sqmake learns between builds command hashes, dependency files read, fingerprints lives in one small state file in the build folder. 3. Describing a build 3.1 A conventional project proposed syntax Templates imply a layout, so a project following one names itself, its kind and what it depends on; sqmake infers its sources and outputs: The C++ standard is not a project's choice: it is the toolchain's §4.3 . 3.2 The escape hatch proposed syntax When a convention does not fit, the same file defines rules and targets: Each of make's pain points has a plain replacement: make sqmake $@ , $< , $^ named parameters: out , ins pattern and implicit rules an explicit map from sources to objects = , := , ?= one assignment, evaluated when it runs tabs and shell quoting commands as argument lists, no shell $ call ... and includes ordinary functions, and require 3.3 Usage requirements decided A library declares, as public or private, the include paths, flags, libraries and modules its users need. A target that links it gets the public ones, and passes on those it re exports. 4. Toolchains 4.1 One toolchain, defined once decided A toolchain is explicit: sqmake never detects compilers. The SDK has one, for every C++ module it builds: clang 23, libc++ 23 and bionic , from sqterm's own llvm , runtimes and sysroot packages on the phone, and from apt.llvm.org's clang 23 with the same sysroot and runtimes on CI. It is defined once, in squared build/toolchain.mk , and the same as toolchain.sh for scripts ; sqmake reads that same definition, so squared's own build and sqmake can never disagree about it. The Android NDK serves only while the SDK moves to that toolchain the plan "One C++23 toolchain" : until the sysroot package carries Android's own API headers and stub libraries. 4.2 The fingerprint decided Every toolchain has a fingerprint : a short hash of the compiler's version, the C++ library's version, the target triple and API level, and every flag that changes a compiled module §4.3 . It names the folder that holds compiled modules §5.2 , and it is part of every command's hash §2.2 . 4.3 Flags that change a compiled module decided These belong to the toolchain, never to a target, and go on every compile and link alike: the C++ standard std=c++23 , the C++ library stdlib=libc++ , the runtime and unwind libraries rtlib=compiler rt , unwindlib=libunwind , threads pthread , bionic's ctype macro D BIONIC CTYPE INLINE=inline and the optimisation level. A target that asks for another value is refused with a plain message naming the flag, before clang's "module file was compiled with ..." can happen. rtlib=compiler rt looks like a link flag, but it turns on target features outline atomics, function multiversioning : given at the link alone, it made CI's clang refuse its own std module sqterm 21, 2026 11 19 . 5. C++ modules 5.1 Order decided Before it compiles, sqmake asks clang scan deps for each source's module dependencies the P1689 format and orders the compiles by them: a module's interface is compiled before what imports it. sqterm's llvm package ships clang scan deps with clang 23. 5.2 Compiled modules decided A compiled module a BMI, .pcm is an output in the graph, like an object file, kept in build/modules/<fingerprint / . A BMI made by another compiler or with other flags is never found there, rather than found and refused. 5.3 The standard library module decided import std is one node per fingerprint: built once from the C++ library's own std.cppm the runtimes package's and shared by every target that imports it. 5.4 Libraries written as modules decided A library written as modules sqcart, sqdrive is vendored as sources and built by its consumer's toolchain. A compiled module never travels between repositories or machines. 6. Running a build 6.1 Stages decided 1. Load: Lua evaluates the build file; it registers toolchains, rules and targets through sqmake's API. 2. Resolve: conventions fill in sources and outputs; usage requirements flow along dependency edges. 3. Plan: a directed acyclic graph of files and commands, module dependencies included §5.1 ; a cycle is refused. 4. Check: each node is marked out of date or not §2.2 . 5. Run: out of date nodes whose inputs are ready run on a thread pool; progress is reported as they finish. 6.2 What it is built from decided C++23 modules, import std . The standard library does the work it can: std::filesystem for paths and times, std::jthread and a queue for parallelism, std::ranges and std::span for the graph, std::expected for each step's result, std::print for output. Custom code is the graph, the dependency file reader and the hash, and each is justified in the developer documentation. Design patterns: Command each step: hashable, loggable, printable by explain , Strategy toolchains , Observer progress and logs, apart from the scheduler , Builder Lua's registration of targets and rules , Factory Context::create . 7. The library and the command line 7.1 Packaging decided libsqmake : the graph, the executor and the Lua bindings. It knows nothing of sqpg or square: they use it, never the reverse. sqmake : a thin command line over the library. A feature the command line needs and the library lacks is a gap in the library. Interface: C++23 modules. A small C interface over them can come later, if a tool in another language needs one. One binary, later: sqpg, sqmake and sqcart may share one binary that dispatches on its name as busybox does . That is packaging, not design: each keeps its own main . 7.2 Lua state decided sqmake works alone and embedded; the host decides who owns the Lua state: Alone the command line, an IDE : sqmake makes a state and closes it when the context goes. Embedded sqpg : sqmake uses the host's state, never closes it, and puts its API in its own sqmake table. Version: create refuses anything but Lua 5.4, as a std::expected error. Sandbox: a build file runs in its own environment table and reaches the host's globals only where the host allows it. 8. Not sqmake's Code with its own build a library built with CMake, say is a prebuilt artifact or one opaque step, never reimplemented. Workspaces, templates and kits are square's and sqpg's; sqmake is told what to build. 9. Risks Growing into CMake. Every concept needs a strong reason §1.1 . Inference hiding behaviour. explain always shows the resolved graph. Dependency files. Incremental builds rely on reading clang's and GCC's dependency files exactly. Full Lua permits unreadable build files. Whether to narrow the API, as Meson narrows its language, is open. 10. Open questions Does sqmake also build squared and the kits, or only a workspace? How much comes from the template, and how much is declared? Do new projects keep plain make until sqmake exists? Which Lua API is stable for other tools? The build file's name build.lua is proposed .

sq android — the platform layer How this project meets Android. Everything here is yours ownership class: seeded — the generator wrote it once and will not overwrite it. This is the expert escape hatch. You should not normally need it. entry.cpp Runs the android native app glue event loop, translates lifecycle and input events into calls on your App , and brings up a rendering surface if a rendering kit was applied. The renderer import is guarded, so this file compiles with no kit at all. That guard is what makes kit.opengl and a future kit.sfml alternatives rather than one of them being baked in. What the device lacks is decided from its API level , read once at start from the configuration NativeActivity already holds AConfiguration getSdkVersion and logged with the process's name as device: API <n , process <name an app with a :console process logs each separately ; the GL driver is logged once as driver: <version ; <renderer ; <vendor when the first context is current. Both reach logcat make logcat , through adb , which is how a device without Termux is read. Each such check costs a comparison, cheaper than reading a cached answer from storage, so nothing is cached. The UI thread. Everything here runs on the glue's thread, but a window's views belong to Android's main thread, so hiding the bars must happen there. The manifest names squared on create as the activity's entry android.app.func name : it runs on the main thread, adds a pipe to that thread's looper, then starts the glue as its own entry would. The glue's thread writes one byte, a job, into the pipe hide bars , show bars , to the background and the main thread runs it: a few JNI calls on the thread they belong to, no Java. Without the manifest line the glue starts alone: the bars stay up, and the rest works. The system bars are hidden immersive unless your app says app.stage.hide bars false : through WindowInsetsController from API 30, the system UI flags from 19. A swipe from the edge shows them for a moment. They are asked for again after each focus a dialog may bring them back . Back at your root screen sends the app to the background moveTaskToBack , as Home does; only a quit quit , app.quit ends it. What Android keeps. When Android asks its save instance state , the App hands it the screen stack, a few hundred bytes; the log says saved state: N bytes, for Android to keep with the activity . At the next start the log says what came back: saved state: N bytes: Android brings the activity back when Android ended the process itself memory, the freezer , and the App shows the screens again; saved state: none: a new launch after a swipe from the recent apps, a quit, a force stop or a reboot, and the App starts fresh. Your model's own save save comes back either way. The safe area the camera cut out, the keyboard, the bars when shown is measured from the window's insets from API 23. Below that, those methods do not exist, and the window's visible frame getWindowVisibleDisplayFrame , API 1 answers instead: some older devices lay the window out under translucent bars, and the Android 5.1 tablet does found 2026 10 19: its clock and battery drew over the Console's x . It is measured on events, never on a timer: for a few frames after a new window, a rotation, the bars hidden or shown, and the keyboard shown or hidden, and every 30 frames while the keyboard is up it can be closed without a word to the app . Typing. NativeActivity gives native code key codes, never characters. android text.cpp turns a key press into the character it types through Java's KeyCharacterMap one JNI call per key press, never per frame , and shows and hides the soft keyboard. entry.cpp hands your App a sq::app::TextInputService set text input service : when a text field takes focus the keyboard shows once every finger is up: one shown while the touch is still going, Android puts away when it ends , tapping it again brings the keyboard back after it was put away, Enter asks for it again some keyboards, CleverKeys among them, put themselves away after Enter with no text view behind them , and each key arrives as a KeyDown event and, if it types something, a TextInput event with Ctrl, Alt or Meta held, the character without them and the modifiers . What does not arrive: an input method's composition accents built from two keys, CJK input, emoji , which needs a Java InputConnection . The volume keys are left to Android. Running in the background BACKGROUND=1 in the Makefile; background.hpp/.cpp . For an app whose work goes on with the app off the screen a shell, a download : app.keep running {.title = ..., .text = ...} in squared main starts a foreground service, dev.squared.ModelService , with a notification saying so, so Android neither freezes nor ends the process; and a swipe from the recent apps no longer starts the app afresh. The notification opens the app when tapped, and has Exit the app gets QuitRequested and quits; with no activity left, the service stops and the process ends and Acquire / Release wakelock the CPU stays on with the screen off . Quitting stops it, as does app.stop running . The service is a shim from squared's tools/dexgen a constructor and three native methods, 812 bytes with the Console's : BACKGROUND=1 packs it as the APK's classes.dex , and gives the APK a copy of your manifest with the service, android:hasCode="true" and the permissions it needs FOREGROUND SERVICE , WAKE LOCK , POST NOTIFICATIONS ; your manifest is not edited. The natives are registered as the activity is made, through its class loader. Android 13 and later ask for the notification permission the first time, while the app is on screen; without it the service still runs, its notification hidden. Without BACKGROUND=1 , keep running returns false and the log says why. The clipboard. entry.cpp also hands your App a sq::app::ClipboardService set clipboard service , after create : sq android::Clipboard , Android's ClipboardManager through the same JNI code. text out reads the whole clip 512 UTF 16 units at a time, on the stack and says its size in UTF 8; set text writes one, labelled with the app's name. An sq::App passes it to its Stage, where a widget reaches it as stage.clipboard . The Console make CONSOLE=app ; see squared's docs/programmer/console.md . A three finger tap anywhere, or on a keyboard, opens and closes it; the gesture is taken before your App sees it fingers already down are released far off screen, so nothing is clicked . While it is open, a gesture that starts on it is its own: tap to type the keyboard shows , drag to scroll back, hold the input row for half a second to paste, x or Back to close. copy puts lines on the clipboard. Every other touch, and every key while it is closed, reaches your App as before. app stop disposes your App and puts a fresh, uncreated one in its place; app start creates it and hands it the surface again, as at launch; app restart does both. The process, the window, the graphics context and the Console stay, so this recovers from a stuck screen or bad state, not from a crash. While stopped, no method of your App is called and the screen is cleared under the Console. In a Console build a create that fails no longer leaves a black window: the Console opens and app start tries again. quit finishes the activity, the same way your quit requested does. From Termux. A Console build also listens for Termux on this phone 127.0.0.1 , a port made from the package name, and a secret your build makes : make console in the project shows the Console's lines as they are written and runs what you type, make console CMD='mem' runs one command. It waits for the app, and reconnects when the app restarts. make console only starts the app with only the Console running: your App is created by app start , so an app that crashes at start can still be reached. The app's own files go through it both ways: ls files , pull files/crash previous.txt saved in build/pulled/ , pull apk , and push <file name typed in make console into the app's files/ ; logcat shows the app's own system log a library that failed to load, a Java exception and libs what it loaded, no adb needed. screens lists your App's screens and panes and what each keeps scrolls, an unfinished edit , as Android would be given them; screens low memory sends Android's low memory event through it. dump runs groups of commands, one a frame: dump sys every system command, gl and display among them , dump memory , dump crash the last crash report, the last run's log, the system log , several at once dump sys crash , dump all ; dump alone lists them. The entry calls console.update every loop turn for it, and wakes every 16 ms while a dump runs with the app in the background. The secret is in the APK, which other apps can read, so this keeps out apps that are not looking for it, no more: dev builds only. Its socket needs the INTERNET permission, which sqterm's manifest carries for every build pkg's downloads . The last run's log. The newest 200 lines are saved to files/log.txt when the app leaves the screen and when it ends; the next launch moves them to log previous.txt , and log previous shows how that run ended a quit , a swipe away . Crash reports. In a Console build a fatal signal a segfault, an abort writes a report to the app's private files, files/crash.txt : the trace, each frame as a library and an offset for addr2line , then the last 40 lines of the log. The next launch shows it in the Console, in red, once, and moves it to crash previous.txt ; crash shows it again. The signal then goes on to the dev log's handler with DEV LOG and to Android's own crash report, so nothing else is lost. AndroidManifest.xml Two deliberate absences: No <uses sdk . minSdkVersion and targetSdkVersion are passed to aapt2 by the build, so make apk SQ MIN SDK=26 retargets without editing a file. Declaring them here too would create two sources of truth, and aapt2 would take this one. SQ MIN SDK default 22 is also what the code is compiled and linked for, so the manifest cannot claim a level the library was not built for. No android:debuggable . How it fits together Shell the model watches the pty's descriptor Telegraph::watch : it sleeps until the shell writes, a key comes, or Android's lifecycle reaches it. What the shell writes is fed to a sq::term::Terminal , and the screen is published whole sq::term::ScreenPublisher . When the shell exits, the terminal says so as Termux does Process completed code N press Enter , or signal N , sets the state term.completed , and drops what is typed after. TerminalView a custom node, Stage::custom reads the newest screen each frame, puts the glyphs it shows into the atlas, and paints: backgrounds, then glyphs, then underlines. Named keys go through sq::term::key bytes , Ctrl and Alt with a character through key text bytes , typed text as it is. A vertical drag scrolls back. Once term.completed is true, Enter calls quit app the App kept by squared main : the model stops, Android closes the activity, and the next launch starts a new shell. Selecting 12.4, in TerminalView : a long press 0.45 s, within 10 units selects the word under the finger, and the finger still down moves its end; on blank space it shows the bar with Paste alone. The ends are sq::term::TextPoint s, the terminal's line numbers the snapshot's top line plus the row , so they stay on their text as more scrolls in. Two handles hang below the ends; a finger within 40 units takes one, and held at the top or bottom edge it scrolls a line each 60 ms. The bar Copy, Paste sits above the selection's first line, or below it at the top. Copy sends do term.copy "from line from column to line to column" ; the Shell answers with Terminal::copy text in the snapshot term.copied , and the widget gives it to stage.clipboard . Paste reads the clipboard whole, makes it sq::term::paste text , and sends it as term.input in pieces of 1 KB as the rings take them, a frame at a time the paste's buffer, about twice its size, is freed when it is sent . A tap elsewhere, or a key, puts the selection away. Pinch zoom 12.6b, in TerminalView : squared's Stage offers a two finger pinch to the widget under it before it zooms the UI, and the terminal takes it TerminalView::pinch : the font's size, in percent of 20 units, is the size at the pinch's start times its scale, to a step of 5 from 50 to 300. Each step makes the glyphs again at the new pixel size the atlas cleared, the texture uploaded whole and sends the new grid as term.size ; between steps nothing happens. The size is the process's a rotation makes the widget again , read from the app's files terminal.font , the percent and a newline at the first fit and written as the fingers lift. The prefix 12.5, prefix.cpp : squared main makes files/home and files/usr/tmp , and calls stage packages : the APK's assets/packages/index against usr/var/lib/sqterm/packages , the one last installed. When they differ, each archive is copied out of the APK mapped: they are stored uncompressed into usr/var/cache/sqterm/ , so the model's thread reads plain files whatever happens to the activity. Its environment: TERM=sqterm , COLORTERM , LANG , HOME , TMPDIR $PREFIX/tmp , where zsh puts here documents , PREFIX , PATH $PREFIX/bin first, then /system/bin , SHELL , SQTERM , and Android's ANDROID DATA and ANDROID ROOT . square The workspace manager of the squared SDK https://squared netizen.github.io/squared netizen/ , and the one tool that knows what a workspace is. sqpg creates a workspace once; from then on square answers every question about it and makes every change to its shape. sq app — your code The user working directory . Everything in it is yours; the generator will not write here again. The one rule No Android headers in this directory. No <android/... , no <EGL/... , no <GLES3/... . The platform layer in sq android/ owns all of that and calls into your App through the interface in app.hpp . Keeping to this means the same App compiles under template.termux.cpp with a different platform layer. It is easy to lose one include at a time, so it is worth checking when you add code. Lifecycle Method When start once, before the first frame resume / pause focus gained and lost resize w, h before the first render, and on rotation render each frame, only while a surface exists touch phase, x, y a touch; return true if handled stop once, on the way out Called from the platform layer on the main thread. None of them may block. Android kills an unresponsive process without warning. pause is the last call you are guaranteed — Android may destroy the process afterwards without calling stop . Save anything you cannot lose there.
